facts.label: Revisão do B1
facts.sub: Revise o present perfect (I’ve lived here for five years), used to (I used to live in Lisbon) e relativas com who, that e which: the man who plays the guitar.

facts.label: Hábitos do passado
facts.sub: Use used to + verbo base para falar de algo que acontecia no passado e já não acontece: I used to live in Lisbon. Na pergunta e na negativa, use use to: Did you use to…? I didn’t use to…

facts.label: Experiência e tempo
facts.sub: Use have/has + particípio para experiências: I’ve never learned an instrument. Para duração, use for e since: I’ve lived here for five years. Pergunte Have you ever…?

compare.ask: I used to live in Lisbon.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “eu morava em Lisboa” e “moro aqui há cinco anos”.
compare.tip: Diga: “I used to live in Lisbon.”
compare.us: Em inglês: I used to live in Lisbon, mas I’ve lived here for five years. Use who para pessoas e that/which para coisas.

pages.title: The living room · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a quiet Sunday afternoon in Boston. Juno and her friend Rui are in her living room. Photos, books and a guitar are on the table. They talk about their lives so far. The old days and the new days are very different. Rui picks up a photo and smiles.

“Rui, you’ve lived in many places. Where did you use to live?” says Juno. “I used to live in Lisbon, but I’ve lived in Boston for five years.” says Rui. “Have you ever missed home? I mean the city that you grew up in.” says Juno.
